author: cli
text: Defect in comment_rot detection (lines 555-563): logic is delta-based, not consistency-based. Sets rot=True whenever prev_logic_hash != current_logic_hash, which cannot distinguish "logic changed away from comments" from "logic changed back to match comments." Once set, the flag persists even when code reverts to a state where comments accurately describe the logic. No automatic path back to False except by changing comment_hash, which is wrong when comments are already correct. Separately: confirm suppresses the rot DISPLAY in attention but does not clear the flag in the index. Needs consistency checking, not just delta detection.

author: cli
text: CORRECTION to the earlier comment_rot note on this coordinate (2026-08-08, author cli), which claimed 'No automatic path back to False'. That is not what the code does. Verified against indexer.py:559-567: if prev_ch != comment_hash the flag is CLEARED (line 563), so editing the comment does reset it. The three branches are: comments changed -> False; comments unchanged AND logic_hash moved -> True; neither -> inherit the previous value. So comment_rot is a DELTA-BASED LATCH, not a consistency check, and the sticky third branch is the real defect surface: fixing the CODE so the comment becomes accurate again leaves the flag True forever, because only a comment edit clears it. The original note's substance (delta vs consistency, no way back from a code-side fix) stands; its absolute claim does not. Read a rot flag as 'logic moved at some point without the comment moving', never as 'this comment is wrong right now'.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.56.0. The occurrence scheme below is unchanged in behaviour - first occurrence bare, then #2, #3 - and coordinate IDs are therefore stable across this release. Two things moved: the suffix is produced by refs.render rather than an f-string here, and for PYTHON the numbering now arrives already applied from the parser, which numbers once and hands the same map to its entity walk and its call attribution. That is what stopped a call inside the third same-named def being attributed to the first stub.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.56.1. The occurrence scheme and the one-producer note below both still hold unchanged. What moved here is the rot rule: module entities no longer produce comment_rot at all, decided in this function so the flag never reaches the data. A module docstring's claims range over its own surface, over behaviour inside its functions, and over other modules entirely - indexer.py's own docstring does all three - so no hash of this file bounds what the check would be checking. The surface-hash alternative was clearable but silently blind to the second kind of claim, which is the worse direction. See CLAUDE.md lesson 12.
